test: delayed renderer module import followed by public UI scope replacement
classification: correctness-only; no timing or performance claim

setup.serviceWorker: server returned 404 for service-worker.js to keep the delayed dynamic module response on the network; navigator.serviceWorker.controller was false

steps: Opened the staged release in a fresh named agent-browser session.
Clicked Sofle v2 copy and waited for the public editor and Generate case button.
Clicked Generate case; the owned server observed the lazy renderer JS request and held its response for 12 seconds.
Before releasing the response, clicked REVIUNG41 copy. A fresh accessibility snapshot showed REVIUNG41, Keyboard PCB, and its component list while the renderer request remained pending.
After the held response returned, waited for module resolution and inspected the DOM, instrumentation counters, and browser errors.

observationsAfterResponse.casePanelState: Add case settings; no generated case canvas

result: The delayed module response completed after the document/scope replacement. The stale canvas was already unmounted, and resolving the old import caused no WebGL context acquisition, renderer lifecycle observer/listener installation, or frame scheduling. This is a focused public-UI confirmation of stale-mount cancellation for the captured root-prefix release assets.
limitations: This was a root-prefix focused race probe with service-worker registration intentionally unavailable; it does not re-verify offline behavior or the subpath.
The probe did not close the browser tab during import. Root-tab-close cleanup remains outside this observation.
Zero renderer allocations are scoped to the old generated-case canvas after import resolution; this makes no claim about general app listeners or other canvases.
